_comment: Pre-generated speech for every FIXED line the Tutor can say.
THESE ARE URLS TO WORLD-READABLE AUDIO IN OUR OWN DEPOT, NOT SECRETS. They serve the
same clips a browser already fetches during a lesson, and they are tracked on purpose —
the precedent is oracle/voices.enrolled.json: the deploy becomes reproducible, a
re-generation becomes a reviewable diff, and nobody has to reconcile 144 files by hand.
WHY IT EXISTS. Every scripted line — the four characters' greetings, the six safety lines,
the closes, the model-down and moderation fallbacks — used to be synthesised and BILLED
again every single time a child heard it. Depot already deduplicated the storage, so not
even the disk grew; only the invoice did. The set is closed (12 texts x 4 characters x 3
locales = 144 clips) and it does not grow with usage, so it is paid for once, ever.
Produced by 'npm run speech:pregenerate -- --confirm', which needs a configured voice
provider and Depot. It makes ZERO network calls without --confirm.
THE KEY IS A CONTENT HASH of the exact text plus the provider's voice fingerprint
(provider, TTS model, enrolled voice id). So editing a scripted line or re-enrolling a
character's voice ORPHANS the old entry rather than playing stale audio for new words: a
cached line is always the line that was actually reviewed. An orphan is a cache miss,
which costs one paid call and then caches — never a silence.
AN EMPTY 'lines' IS A VALID STATE and is what ships until the script is run against a
real deployment. The runtime falls through to the Redis cache and then to a paid call.
Run 'npm run speech:pregenerate' (no --confirm) to see what is missing or stale.
